headline_observations: Ordering defies the naive expectation (blive high, btest low, research zero): research projects score mid-high via RESEARCH-NATIVE instruments (pre-registration, notation sheets, kill rules, adversarial review) — the boundary claim refines to 'different artifact types and lifecycle', not 'no substrate'.
btest at 12 is not flat: commit-ID discipline was real during the SMIM era and measurably decayed after extraction (temporal within-project evidence, stronger than cross-project).
datacli (16/24 at 117 files) = a-la-carte adoption keeping cheap high-payoff elements, skipping ceremony — consistent with the complexity-threshold claim.
b-autobot and blive have INVERSE profiles (guardrails+validation vs representation+session) — the four practices are separable in practice, not a package.
seamQ shows substrate-as-scaffolding: erected during work, deliberately torn down at publication.
